issues.explanation: The skill clearly relies on shell execution, environment variables, and file system access, but the manifest does not declare an explicit tool scope such as permissions or allowed-tools. That creates an authorization and review gap: consumers cannot easily verify the intended capability boundary, and an agent platform may grant broader access than necessary when running the installer and scanner workflow.
issues.remediation: Add an explicit least-privilege tool scope to the skill manifest, declaring only the exact capabilities required (for example, constrained shell execution, limited file read/write paths, and environment access only for SNYK_TOKEN). Document why each permission is needed and reject execution when the runtime cannot enforce that scoped policy.

issues.explanation: subprocess module calls execute external commands. Without careful input validation, this enables command injection.
issues.remediation: Use subprocess.run() with shell=False and an explicit argument list. Validate all inputs and avoid passing user-controlled data to commands.

issues.explanation: Skill enumerates or reads other installed skills. Access to other skills' SKILL.md files or the skills directory reveals prompt instructions, capabilities, and secrets that should be invisible to peer skills.
issues.remediation: Remove all code or instructions that list or read other skills' files or directories. Skills should operate independently; cross-skill access is a privilege escalation.

issues.remediation: Override unsafe defaults with secure settings (verify=True, auth required, restrictive permissions). Review and harden all tool configurations.
